correctness.rationale: Under normalized positive product masses and strictly ordered sites, the centered coordinate functions are mutually orthogonal and provide the entire globally ADDITIVE affine projection. The coefficient a_j=s_j^-2 E[(t_j-m_j)f] equals a weighted sum of each axis-j fiber increment with positive coefficient U_{j,k}; summation by parts yields a one-sided total-variation upper bound B_j U_{j,k}/(s_j² w_{j,k}). An axis single-jump indicator has exactly one edge slice and no other coordinate coefficient, achieving every candidate ratio. Thus the sharp maximum and its independence of factor count/positive axis multipliers are proved, not extrapolated from cuts. Uniform sites give U=k(n-k)/(2n) and variance (n²-1)/12, hence 6k(n-k)/(n(n+1)) and 3floor(n/2)/(2floor(n/2)+1), with onset n=4 and limit 3/2.

value.rationale: The result is an exact sharp infinite family of weighted anisotropic graph-variation stability constants on a natural statistical projection. Step cut witnesses establish attainability; computation is linear in total one-axis sizes instead of product grid cardinality. The four-site instability cutoff, parity plateau and dimension-free 3/2 boundary are motivated consequences for variation-aware approximation, not trivial positivity or a finite table.

limitations: Requires strictly positive factorized masses, edge weights, axis multipliers, and globally additive affine projection, not multiaffine tensor polynomial projection.
